note: Recast from the original description of Emerson 1952 (in English); only the soldier is described there and neither the alate nor the worker is described. The measurements are taken from table 3 of the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is distinguished from all other species of the genus by the three sharp projections of the labrum, whose lateral corners form an angle of about 50—60° and whose apex is more acute than a right angle; closest to araujoi, from which it differs in the sharper lateral points of the labrum, the straighter and more parallel sides of the head, the more concave sides of the postmentum and the relatively shorter hind tibia. Antenna 13—14 segments, segment 3 occasionally showing signs of subdivision.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Abdominal tergites slightly paler yellow than the head. Head, pronotum and abdominal tergites with scattered setae, sparser on the head, and with a few almost invisible short hairs on the head and pronotum; anterior margin and surface of the pronotum with short hairs. Head fairly large, thick and long, the sides nearly straight and parallel, the posterior margin and posterior corners rounded. Frontal tube relatively small, from above only just reaching the base of the postclypeus (the suture between the postclypeus and the frons is indistinct). The narrowest part of the postmentum lies in the middle or at the basal third, the sides slightly concave. Antenna 13—14 segments, segment 3 showing signs of splitting in some specimens. Lateral corners of the labrum sharp, forming an angle of about 50—60°, the apex more acute than a right angle. Mandibles as in figure 9. Anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Measurements: head including mandibles 3.09—3.23, head length to the tip of the frontal tube 2.00—2.19, head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 2.07—2.29, head width 1.45—1.59, head thickness 1.23—1.41, frontal tube length 0.21—0.27, labrum width 0.47—0.53, left mandible length 1.12—1.23, right mandible length from the notch 0.65—0.77, postmentum widest 0.50—0.56 and narrowest 0.35—0.45, pronotum length 0.50—0.56 and width 0.93—1.06, hind tibia length 1.12—1.24 mm (n=8—10). Type locality Corumbá, Mato Grosso, Brazil (19°07′S, 57°38′W); the soldier syntypes were collected by Silvestri in 1900.
